1	# @frtnbach/node-red-contrib-mcp-server
2	
3	Generic [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server nodes for
4	Node-RED: expose any flow as an MCP tool behind an OAuth-protected endpoint, with optional
5	Node-RED admin (flow read/deploy) tools. No home-automation or other domain coupling — this
6	is a bare building block for turning Node-RED flows into MCP tools that AI assistants
7	(Claude, etc.) can call.
8	
9	## Nodes
10	
11	- **`mcp-server`** (config node) — hosts a standalone MCP JSON-RPC endpoint at
12	  `POST /mcp/<path>`, OAuth 2.0 protected-resource discovery (RFC 9728), authorization-server
13	  discovery (RFC 8414) proxying a real OIDC identity provider, and a dynamic client
14	  registration shim, so OAuth-aware MCP clients (e.g. Claude.ai) can self-register and
15	  authenticate. Multiple `mcp-server` nodes can coexist, each with its own path and its own
16	  independent auth configuration.
17	- **`mcp-in`** — defines one MCP tool (name, description, JSON-Schema parameters). When an
18	  MCP client calls the tool, the node emits a message carrying the call arguments; wire the
19	  rest of the flow to do the actual work.
20	- **`mcp-out`** — resolves a pending tool call. Wire the end of your flow here with
21	  `msg._mcpCallId` intact (from the originating `mcp-in` message) and `msg.payload` set to
22	  the result.
23	
24	A single `mcp-in` → ... → `mcp-out` chain is one MCP tool. Build as many chains as you want
25	against the same `mcp-server` node to expose a whole toolset.
26	
27	## Admin tools
28	
29	Enable **Admin tools** on an `mcp-server` node to additionally expose two tools that operate
30	on Node-RED's own Admin HTTP API, gated by a configurable JWT claim (default: `groups`
31	contains `admin`):
32	
33	- **`get_flow`** — lists all flow tabs (id, label, node count), or returns the full JSON of
34	  one tab when called with an `id`.
35	- **`deploy_flow`** — creates or updates a flow tab.
36	
37	## Configuring an `mcp-server` node
38	
39	- **General**: name, `path` (→ registers `POST /mcp/<path>`), the public `Server URL` this
40	  Node-RED instance is reachable at, optional server name/instructions shown to the model, and
41	  an optional **hostname filter** (see below).
42	- **Auth**: an OIDC `Identity provider` issuer URL (**required** — endpoints auto-discovered
43	  from `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, with PocketID-style fallback paths; leaving this
44	  empty produces a broken OAuth discovery document with relative-path endpoints and no working
45	  auth, so the editor won't let you deploy without it), client id/secret (leave the secret
46	  empty to run as a public/PKCE client — recommended), **required** redirect URIs (defaults to
47	  Claude.ai's callback), scopes, token audience, an optional local debug token that bypasses
48	  the IdP entirely for local testing (put any placeholder URL in Identity provider and rely on
49	  the debug token — it's never contacted when the debug token matches), and a whole-server
50	  **required claim/value gate** (see below, unrelated despite the similar name).
51	- **Admin**: enable/disable admin tools, admin token (for the Node-RED Admin API), admin API
52	  port, and the required claim/value gate that additionally restricts just the admin tools.
53	
54	### Access control
55	
56	Two independent, optional gates:
57	
58	- **Whole-server gate** (Auth tab, `Required claim`/`Required value`): when a value is set, the
59	  validated token's claim must contain it for *any* of this server's tools — including admin
60	  tools — to be usable. Callers who fail the check still connect (`initialize` succeeds) but see
61	  no tools and any `tools/call` is refused with a human-readable reason. Leave the value empty
62	  (the default) to allow all authenticated users.
63	- **Admin-only gate** (Admin tab): the same shape, but only gates `get_flow`/`deploy_flow` —
64	  ordinary tools defined by `mcp-in`/`mcp-out` remain usable by anyone who passes the
65	  whole-server gate above.
66	
67	Both denials are returned as an MCP tool result with `isError: true` and an explanatory message
68	(not a raw JSON-RPC protocol error), so the reason reaches the calling model instead of being
69	collapsed into a generic "tool execution failed".
70	
71	### Hostname filtering
72	
73	Off by default. When **Only serve requests for this hostname** is enabled, the node only answers
74	requests whose `Host` header matches the hostname in its `Server URL`. This lets several
75	`mcp-server` nodes share the *same* `path` on one Node-RED instance, each answering only its own
76	virtual host — useful behind a reverse proxy that fronts multiple hostnames for one Node-RED
77	backend. Leave it off for a single server, or when a reverse proxy rewrites the `Host` header.
78	
79	### Reverse proxy
80	
81	Each `mcp-server` node is its own OAuth resource — unlike a single shared MCP endpoint, every
82	instance registers **its own** discovery and registration routes, scoped under its `path`. For
83	a node with `path: docker` and `Server URL: https://mcp.example.com`, these six routes exist:
84	
85	| Method & path | Purpose |
86	|---|---|
87	| `POST /mcp/docker` | The JSON-RPC MCP endpoint (bearer-token protected) |
88	| `GET /mcp/docker/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` | Resource metadata (RFC 9728), path-inserted form |
89	| `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/docker` | Resource metadata (RFC 9728), RFC 8414 form |
90	| `GET /mcp/docker/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | Auth-server metadata (RFC 8414), path-inserted form |
91	| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/docker` | Auth-server metadata (RFC 8414), RFC 8414 form |
92	| `POST /mcp/docker/oauth/register` | Dynamic client registration shim |
93	
94	Both well-known forms are advertised because different MCP clients probe different ones —
95	expose both. Since every instance's routes share the `/mcp/<path>` and `/.well-known/*/mcp/<path>`
96	shapes, **one set of wildcard rules covers every current and future `mcp-server` node** (as long
97	as they're all reachable through the same domain/upstream) — no reverse-proxy change needed when
98	adding a new `path`. Example, using
99	[Caddy](https://caddyserver.com/) via [caddy-docker-proxy](https://github.com/lucaslorentz/caddy-docker-proxy)
100	labels:
101	
102	```yaml
103	labels:
104	  caddy_1: mcp.example.com
105	  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_0: /mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
106	  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_1: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
107	  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_2: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
108	```
109	
110	Node-RED itself 404s any path that isn't an actual registered route, so the wildcard doesn't
111	expose anything beyond what each deployed `mcp-server` node already registers. If a `path`
112	needs to be reachable on a *different* domain than the others, give it its own `caddy_N` site
113	block (or combine with [hostname filtering](#hostname-filtering) above).
114	
115	**What the identity provider needs to support** (same requirements as `lib/mcp-auth.js`):
116	
117	- An **OIDC provider with discovery** — endpoints are read from
118	  `‹issuerUrl›/.well-known/openid-configuration`, falling back to PocketID's path layout if
119	  discovery is unavailable.
120	- **JWT access tokens** signed with a key published on the provider's **JWKS** (tokens are
121	  verified locally; opaque/introspection-only access tokens are not supported).
122	- A client configured with the **redirect URI(s)** from the node's *Redirect URIs* setting,
123	  grant types `authorization_code` + `refresh_token`, **PKCE (S256)**, and — if a client secret
124	  is set — `client_secret_post` auth. Leave the secret empty to run as a public/PKCE client
125	  (recommended).
126	
127	> Tested with **Caddy** (reverse proxy) + **PocketID** (identity provider) + **Claude.ai** (MCP
128	> client). Any spec-compliant OIDC provider issuing JWT access tokens, behind any reverse proxy
129	> that forwards the routes above, should work the same way.
130	
131	## Examples
132	
133	See [`examples/`](examples/) for nine ready-to-import flows (Jellyfin, Calibre, Docker,
134	Music Assistant, Radarr, iRobot/rest980, Overseerr, Sonarr, Spotify), each with its own
135	`mcp-server` node (server description pre-filled, `Server URL`/`Identity provider` left
136	blank for you to fill in) and `mcp-in`/`mcp-out` tools — a good reference for wiring up
137	your own tools.
138	
139	## Development
140	
141	```
142	npm install
143	npm test
144	```

Kollat igenom hela paketet. Läget är faktiskt riktigt bra — 49 tester gröna, paketet packar rent (27 filer, 50 kB), inga hårdkodade hemligheter eller riktiga hostnamn läcker i example-flödena (allt går via `env.get(...)`, enda absoluta URL:erna är publika API:er och en `your-nodered-host`-platshållare). Snyggt hantverk.

Men det finns ett par saker att ta innan vi trycker på knappen.

## Måste fixas (annars vägrar npm)

**1. `"private": true` i package.json** — det här stoppar `npm publish` helt. Måste bort.

**2. Scoped paket + publik access** — `@frtnbach/...` är scoped, och scoped paket defaultar till *restricted* (kräver betalplan). Första publiceringen behöver antingen `npm publish --access public` eller, snyggare och permanent:
```json
"publishConfig": { "access": "public" }
```

## Borde fixas (kvalitet/metadata)

**3. Saknar `repository`, `bugs`, `homepage`** — npm rekommenderar det, och det ger en vettig npm-sida + länk tillbaka till repot. Just nu finns inget alls.

**4. Ingen `files`-allowlist** — npm varnar (`gitignore-fallback`). Det funkar, men en explicit `files` är framtidssäker så inget oväntat (t.ex. `.claude/`) råkar följa med senare. Frågan är också om du vill ha med `test/` i tarballen — det är ~24 kB brus som slutanvändaren inte behöver. `examples/` vill vi behålla, de refereras i README.

## Icke-blockare

**5. `npm audit`** flaggar `serialize-javascript` via `mocha` — men det är bara en devDependency, den skeppas aldrig. Ingen fara. Kan bumpas vid tillfälle men inget release-stopp.

En liten sak till: repot ligger på branchen `master` (hal2 är på `main`). Bara värt att notera, inget problem.

---

Vill du att jag fixar 1–4 i package.json? Mitt förslag:

- Ta bort `private`
- Lägg till `publishConfig.access: public`
- Lägg till `repository`/`bugs`/`homepage` (behöver din GitHub-URL — vad är den?)
- Lägg till `files`-allowlist: `["nodes/", "lib/", "examples/", "README.md", "LICENSE"]` (utan `test/`)

Säg bara till om GitHub-URL:en och om du vill ha kvar tester i paketet, så snickrar jag ihop det.

GitHub-URL: https://github.com/flic/node-red-contrib-mcp-server

Tester bör inte följa med i paketet.

Kör 1-4
